\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആരും} (āruṁ)}{ആരും (āruṁ)}]{\ml{ആരും} (āruṁ) — nobody (with a negative verb)}

\label{lesson:ML-C177-arum}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to fall, then the Malayalam for to live.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആരും}}
\textbf{\ml{ആരും}} — \emph{āruṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}nobody (with a negative verb)\textquotedblright{}. Malayalam negates a verb by joining \textbf{\ml{ഇല്ല}} (\emph{illa}) onto it: \textbf{\ml{ആരും} \ml{വന്നില്ല}} — \emph{āruṁ vannilla} — \textquotedblleft{}Nobody came.\textquotedblright{} To say something is not a thing, it uses \textbf{\ml{അല്ല}} (\emph{alla}): \textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{എന്റെ} \ml{വീട്} \ml{അല്ല}} — \emph{itŭ enṟe vīṭŭ alla} — \textquotedblleft{}This is not my house.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āruṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āruṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{āruṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to fall, then the Malayalam for to live, then say \emph{āruṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആരെങ്കിലും} (āreṅkiluṁ)}{ആരെങ്കിലും (āreṅkiluṁ)}]{\ml{ആരെങ്കിലും} (āreṅkiluṁ) — anyone, someone}

\label{lesson:ML-C177-arenkilum}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for never, then the Malayalam for nowhere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആരെങ്കിലും}}
\textbf{\ml{ആരെങ്കിലും}} — \emph{āreṅkiluṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}anyone, someone\textquotedblright{}. A yes-or-no question ends in \textbf{-\ml{ഓ}} (\emph{-ō}): \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} becomes \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ടോ}}. \textbf{\ml{അവിടെ} \ml{ആരെങ്കിലും} \ml{ഉണ്ടോ}?} — \emph{aviṭe āreṅkiluṁ uṇṭō?} — \textquotedblleft{}Is anyone there?\textquotedblright{}
